q-216986.name: Question 1
q-216986.worked_solution:
We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}(3{x}^{4}+4) & = \\ 2{x}^{2}\cdot (3{x}^{4})+2{x}^{2}\cdot 4 & = \\ 6{x}^{2+4}+8{x}^{2} & = \\ 6{x}^{6}+8{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

?

6x3(x2−x33)=

a
x4+2x3
b
3x4+x6
c
x4+x6
d
3x4−2x6
e
2x2−2x6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

6x3(x2−x33)=(6x3)(x2)+(6x3)(−x33)=(6x3)(12x)+(6x3)(−13x3)=(6⋅12)(x3⋅x)+(6⋅(−13))(x3⋅x3)=(3)(x3+1)+(−2)⋅(x3+3)=3x4−2x6

q-44735.worked_solution:
We multiply each term inside the parentheses by the term outside the parentheses, simplify using the rules of exponents, and then we add the results together:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{p}^{4}(-7{p}^{5}{q}^{2}+3{p}^{2}{q}^{5}) & = \\ (-{p}^{4})(-7{p}^{5}{q}^{2})+(-{p}^{4})(3{p}^{2}{q}^{5}) & = \\ (\,(-1)\cdot (-7)\,)({p}^{4}\cdot {p}^{5})({q}^{2})+(\,(-1)\cdot 3)({p}^{4}\cdot {p}^{2})({q}^{5}) & = \\ (7)({p}^{4+5})({q}^{2})+(-3)({p}^{4+2})({q}^{5}) & = \\ 7{p}^{9}{q}^{2}-3{p}^{6}{q}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$
